GOOGL.rationale: Alphabet delivered a blowout Q2 2026 quarter with revenue up 24% YoY to $119.8B, EPS of $9.11 (vs ~$2.90 expected, though ~$98B of the net income beat came from unrealized equity gains on SpaceX), and Google Cloud surging 82% YoY to $24.8B with operating income tripling. The core advertising business remains healthy with Search revenue up 17% and YouTube ads up 13%. However, the massive capex increase to $195-205B for 2026 (up from $180-190B) turned free cash flow negative at -$5.8B in Q2, and management warned of ~$20B annual depreciation starting in 2027. The stock has pulled back ~20% from its 2026 peak, and at a P/E of ~19x (vs 33-39x range over the past year), it is clearly cheap vs its own recent history. The balance sheet remains fortress-like with $242.5B cash and $640B equity. Key risks include antitrust structural remedies (DOJ Chrome/Android divestiture risk), Gemini 3.5 Pro delays, and margin pressure from AI spending. The near-term catalyst is the Q2 earnings beat and subsequent re-rating as the market digests the cloud backlog of $514B and the massive capex as demand-driven rather than speculative. Berkshire Hathaway's $31B position and Warren Buffett's personal endorsement provide institutional validation.
key_factors: Q2 2026 revenue +24% YoY to $119.8B; 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth
Google Cloud revenue +82% YoY to $24.8B with operating margin expanding to 35.6%; backlog at $514B
P/E of ~19x is near the bottom of its 12-month range (18.1-39.5x), clearly cheap vs own history
Massive capex guidance raised to $195-205B for 2026, turning FCF negative; ~$20B annual depreciation starting 2027
Fortress balance sheet: $242.5B cash, $640B equity, debt-to-equity of 0.16
Antitrust risk: DOJ structural remedies including potential Chrome/Android divestiture
Gemini 3.5 Pro delays and AI competition from OpenAI/Anthropic
Berkshire Hathaway's $31B position; Buffett personally initiated the investment
EPS of $9.11 includes ~$98B unrealized gain on SpaceX equity stake; operating income +30% to $40.8B
Search revenue +17% to $63.3B; YouTube ads +13% to $11.1B; core ad business healthy

sources_cited.excerpt: Alphabet raised its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195-205 billion, with about 60% going to servers that depreciate over six years. This will result in approximately $20 billion in annual depreciation expense starting in 2027

Alphabet stock fell 6.6% despite crushing Q2 earnings expectations with $9.11 EPS (vs. $2.88 expected) and $119.8B revenue (vs. $116.5B expected). The decline was driven by investor concerns over massive AI capital investments of $195-205B this year, which have turned the company's free cash flow negative at -$5.8B in Q2
Berkshire Hathaway has significantly increased its stake in Alphabet to nearly $31 billion, making it the conglomerate's fifth-largest holding
securities fraud investigation into Alphabet Inc. has been launched following Bloomberg's report that Google is months behind schedule on delivering its Gemini 3.5 Pro AI model

Google Cloud backlog jumped over $50 billion sequentially to $514 billion; operating cash flow of $39.1 billion for the quarter and $185.7 billion over the trailing 12 months; Q2 capital expenditures of $44.9 billion driving negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion
